name: btc_regime_timeliness_first_20260808
created: 2026-08-08T (written BEFORE any OOS read of this candidate)
why_this_contract_exists: The early-wave research round found exactly one lever that buys early-wave accuracy for free: a causal turn-suspect routing overlay at boost 0.5 raises first-quintile agreement from 34.0% to 49.8% on VAL while leaving total agreement unchanged at 70.1%. It failed the standing selection gate on ONE criterion only -- median run 5 bars against a floor of 8. That floor was chosen for a STABILITY-first labelling objective (half of the oracle's 16-bar median wave). Lowering it inside that contract would be post-hoc goalpost-shifting, so this separate contract states a TIMELINESS-first objective and derives its own floor from principle. The OOS window has NOT been read for this candidate; that read happens once, after this file is written.
objective: Label the current wave direction as EARLY AS POSSIBLE after a turn, without giving up total accuracy and without degenerating into per-bar noise.

candidate.form: post-processing OVERLAY on the frozen detector -- the frozen model is not retrained and remains intact underneath
candidate.turn_suspect_state: causal zigzag at theta=0.001 disagrees with causal zigzag at theta=0.005 (both nonzero). Causal: both are online state machines. Active on 46.1% of VAL bars and covers 54.6% of first-quintile bars.
candidate.overlay: logit(p) := logit(p_frozen) + 0.5 * czz(0.001) on turn-suspect bars, unchanged elsewhere
candidate.decode: unchanged: jump-penalized causal online DP, lambda=0.5
candidate.boost_value_is_fixed: 0.5 is NOT swept here. It is the unique point in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} with ZERO total-accuracy cost on VAL (70.1 vs 68.2 vs 65.3), which is what the objective 'buy earliness only where it is free' selects. No further tuning.

run_floor_derivation.principle_1: a run shorter than the detector's own post-pivot detection lag (3-4 bars) would flip before the turn it claims could have been confirmed, i.e. pure noise
run_floor_derivation.principle_2: one quarter of the theta=0.005 oracle's 16-bar median wave
run_floor_derivation.note: both principles independently give 4 bars. The stability-first contract's floor of 8 (half a wave) is retained for that contract; it is not amended.

adoption_gates_single_oos_read.gate_1_no_accuracy_regression: OOS total agreement >= 67.0 (frozen model's OOS 68.0 minus at most 1.0pp)
adoption_gates_single_oos_read.gate_2_timeliness_gain_persists: OOS first-quintile agreement >= 38.8 (frozen model's OOS Q1 30.8 plus at least half of the +15.8pp VAL gain)
adoption_gates_single_oos_read.gate_4_not_a_phase_artifact: lag-profile peak lag >= 0 bars. Mandatory because the same research round produced a candidate with a spectacular Q1 (84.1%) that turned out to be a phase shift into noise (peak agreement 53.2% at -66 bars). A leading peak here would mean the Q1 gain is positional, not informational.
adoption_gates_single_oos_read.gate_5_detection_lag: OOS median post-pivot detection lag <= the frozen model's 3 bars

if_adopted: Kept ALONGSIDE the stability-first frozen detector, not replacing it: two detectors for two jobs. Stability-first (8-bar runs) for regime labelling and charting where flicker is costly; timeliness-first for early-turn detection. Both recipes live in their own frozen-config JSONs and downstream code must name which one it reads.
if_it_fails: The lever is closed. No re-tuning of boost, lambda, or the floor on this validation window.
scope_limit: This is a DETECTOR contract, not a trading contract. Nothing here claims tradeable edge: the theta=0.005 median wave amplitude (0.97%) is below the 2x0.5% confirmation cost, and a 4-5 bar median run implies heavy turnover. Promotion to any entry/sizing role requires its own contract with PnL gates.
